name: IL-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+5 partisan lean in a favorable Democratic environment
Heavy Democratic outside spending (~$5.5M) backing Melissa Bean
Open seat after Krishnamoorthi's retirement removes incumbency advantage
Prediction markets price the Democratic nominee near 94%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly Democratic: a D+5 district, a strong national environment, and Bean outraising Davis with massive outside support on her side. The open seat and absence of any polling add some uncertainty, but nothing in the evidence suggests a competitive race.
model.watch: Any late general-election polling or a shift in the national environment toward Republicans would be the first sign this open seat could tighten.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Raja Krishnamoorthi (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Democrats defend a suburban Chicago seat opening up after Raja Krishnamoorthi's retirement to run for Senate. The district carries a D+5 partisan lean, and the national environment this cycle has favored Democrats, giving the party a solid structural edge even without an incumbent on the ballot.

Melissa Bean, a former congresswoman, has raised about $2.1 million and benefits from roughly $5.5 million in outside support, far outmatching Republican Jennifer Davis's $1.5 million in fundraising. Prediction markets price the Democratic side around 94 percent. With no public polling available, the forecast leans on fundamentals and spending, both of which point to a comfortable Democratic hold, though the open-seat nature of the race leaves a wider band of uncertainty than a typical incumbent defense.
